title: TrailGenic Running Conditioning Dataset
description: Canonical aggregate plus selected-session TrailGenic conditioning module for fasted running. Shorter run/walk sessions, matched-distance steady sessions, and the intentional max-speed interval session are separate analytic contexts. It does not expose raw telemetry.
correction_notice: Heart-rate drift values were corrected on 2026-08-18. Prior drift values and derived interpretations are superseded. Drift is descriptive and is not a measure of metabolic flexibility or running economy.

shorter_run_walk.comparison_rule: Compare only within the shorter-distance context.

max_speed_intervals.comparison_rule: Declared maximal interval block S15–17; whole-session values include walking recovery.

mixed_run_walk.comparison_rule: Mixed run/walk; maximum-speed intent and work/recovery splits are not inferred.

records.mechanism: The HR-per-mile proxy is distance- and protocol-dependent, so running comparisons require matched distance and session design.

aggregate_finding.cross_context_warning: HR-per-mile is distance- and protocol-dependent. Cross-context values are not direct measures of running economy.

summary_statistics.recovery_observation: 16 ready; 4 not ready; 0 missing. Source labels, not verified recovery.

methodology.metric_formula: HR-per-mile proxy = average heart rate / distance in miles
methodology.comparison_frame: S1–5 shorter run/walk; S6–14 historical steady run/walk; S15–17 declared max-speed intervals; S18–20 mixed run/walk.
methodology.session_15_boundary: Very humid max-speed intervals with walking recovery; not a steady-state comparison.
methodology.claim_boundary: Conditioning tracking only. Corrected HR drift and HR-per-mile values are descriptive and do not establish metabolic flexibility, running economy, biological age, causality, or clinical efficacy.

claims: 20 entries through September 17; S15–17 declared maximal intervals and S18–20 mixed run/walk remain separate.
S20: 3.23 miles in 39.3 minutes, HR 148/178 bpm, -2.0% drift, load 79, and a not-ready source flag.
Versus S19, S20 pace was about 5.6% faster while average HR rose 2 bpm and device load rose from 66 to 79. This is not proof of improved efficiency.
S17–20 are marked not ready; timing and physiological basis of the flags are not established.

source_provenance.filename: Trailgenic World Model Datasets - MASTER Values Only - Sep1726.xlsx
source_provenance.charter: TG World Model Datasets Charter v1.0 — September 2026
source_provenance.author: Mike Ye
source_provenance.interpretation: Ella; final judgment remains with Mike Ye

evidence_labels.recorded: Field entries and wearable outputs; device estimates are not laboratory measurements.
evidence_labels.unmeasured: No autophagy measurement; no recovery outcome inferred from missing follow-up.

recovery_field_boundary: Ready/not-ready are source classifications with unspecified timing and method; they do not independently establish post-session recovery.

data_quality_notes.detail: Run S20 has numeric 48 in the HR Drift Audit row. It is not used as drift or another physiological measurement; corrected drift is -2.0%.

decision_rule.rule: Consolidate the mixed run/walk dose; obtain timed recovery and comparable work/recovery splits before escalating maximum-effort volume.
